title: promote-latest.mjs fails the run on npm read lag after every write succeeded, so the GitHub Release is left uncut (paired with quest-cli QCLI-465)
description:
Twin of quest-cli QCLI-465 (opum-ai/quest-cli#530), filed the way LCLI-621/QCLI-400 were paired. Found by the 0.13.0 promotion (LCLI-665) on 2026-10-07.

promote-latest.mjs moved every dist-tag — the six platforms by dist-tag, and the launcher published onto latest from opum-ai-lore-0.13.0.tgz — and then its own post-write verification failed the run at exit 1 while npm read lag was still resolving, printing: "@opum-ai/lore: latest reads 0.12.0, expected 0.13.0" and "The writes returned success but the registry does not serve latest = 0.13.0 everywhere after 10 reads." The writes were CORRECT — the orchestrator read the registry minutes later and latest was 0.13.0 on all seven, with the launcher dist.integrity and shasum identical to the final tarball from that run — but the process had already exited 1.

Because that verification sits before them, two steps never ran: ensureGitHubRelease (the GitHub Release had to be repaired out of band, and the repair then failed on an upstream HTTP 500) and the README read-back. The record file scripts/release-0.13.0/latest-rollback.json was written and was not used.

The fix shape is the one quest-cli adopted: the post-write verification should WAIT OUT registry read lag the way the README read-back already does, instead of failing the run on a transient read. Worth deciding too: whether a read-lag failure should exit 3 (promotion complete, a post-latest step outstanding) rather than 1, which now reads as a failed promotion when the promotion in fact succeeded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: promote-latest.mjs waits out registry read lag in its post-write verification, so a promotion whose writes all succeeded completes in one run rather than exiting 1 while the npm read API catches up
On a run whose writes all succeeded, the GitHub Release is cut by ensureGitHubRelease and the README read-back runs, with neither left to an out-of-band repair

implementationNotes:
SECOND WAY THE RELEASE STEP IS LEFT UNCUT (team-lead, 2026-10-07). The out-of-band repair is itself fallible. node scripts/github-release.mjs --version 0.13.0 --create returned exit 1 with "could not create release v0.13.0: HTTP 500 (https://api.github.com/repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/releases)", and nothing was created: gh release view v0.13.0 says "release not found" and v0.12.0 is still Latest. So as of this writing the 0.13.0 GitHub Release is still uncut, for the second reason. The 500 is upstream and not the payload: GitHub was partly degraded from about 15:07Z, with check-runs and commit-status returning 500 in other repositories too while release listing still worked, and the same outage later rejected a git push with "remote rejected (Internal Server Error)". The promote preflight had accepted the identical inputs minutes earlier, saying it would create release v0.13.0 "Lore CLI 0.13.0" (11887 bytes of notes), marked latest. Worth weighing when this task is fixed: a single read-lag failure should not require an out-of-band repair whose own failure mode ALSO leaves the release uncut, and the repair is not retried automatically.
REVIEW VERDICT, recorded verbatim. Unit: lore-cli-review-633-ea037d0, model claude-opus-5-5 (read from its transcript by team-lead). Head reviewed: ea037d0c6bd0a20dcc264e4861b01cf0b4208061. Worktree: .claude/worktrees/review-633-ea037d0. Source file sha256 prefix 727eea2582c8c37c, 9025 bytes. Exit-code ruling (team-lead): keep exit 1 on non-convergence. Round 1 fixes landed on the PR branch at aee74ef4; NOTE 11 is filed as a follow-up, not built.

VERDICT lore-cli#633 @ ea037d0c: APPROVE

AC0 and AC1 hold by file read, and none of the findings below blocks either one. Reviewer unit (read-only, model claude-opus-5-5), detached worktree at ea037d0c6bd0a20dcc264e4861b01cf0b4208061. I had no shell, so nothing was run and no diff was taken.

FINDINGS

1. NOTE — scripts/promote-latest.mjs:663 (also the test comment at test/promote-latest.test.ts:3295). Claim 2's reasoning is wrong, though the guard is still worth having. To the question "can any input give zero reads and a pass": no.
   - verifyTags (:690) and verifyFinalLauncher (:1119) both return ok:false when their loop never runs. This holds for attempts of 0, a negative number, or NaN, and for an explicit verifyOptions.attempts too, so zero reads fail closed. They do not pass.
   - What the guard really prevents is an unexplained exit 1. On --rollback, a restore that succeeded would reach `if (!check.ok) return 1` at :1889 with an empty `wrong` list, so nothing would be printed.
   - Fix: reword both comments to say zero reads fail with no explanation.

2. MINOR — test/promote-latest.test.ts:3304-3305. The converging test's two side assertions can be satisfied without STEP 7 succeeding.
   - The step-9 preflight already calls `gh release view`, as the tests at :2778 show. So `c[1] === "release"` is true before any write.
   - The text "README read-back" also appears in the :1947 line ("a README read-back result is never a reason…"), which prints before ensureGitHubRelease runs.
   - Only `code === 0` carries the claim. It is reachable only through :2001, which needs githubRelease.ok and a PASSED read-back, so the test is not vacuous today. Its stated assertions just don't prove what their names say.
   - It is also not vacuous on lag: it relies on its pair, where lagReads 3 fails "after 3 reads", which proves the stale reads land inside STEP 7.
   - Fix: assert `c[2] === "create"`, as :3314 already does, and assert that a `bash README_READBACK_SCRIPT` call was made.

3. MINOR — scripts/promote-latest.mjs:1509-1510, 1518-1525, 1883-1887. --rollback now reads REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS but never validates it.
   - The comment at :1509-1510 ("--rollback runs no read-back, so it does not read the variable") is now false: waitOptions, derived from the window, feeds the rollback's verifyTags.
   - An invalid "30m" gives a single read, where the default would give 121.
   - "1e12" passes Number() as finite and gives about 6.7e10 reads, which is effectively unbounded if a restored tag never reads back.
   - On --promote the window is validated (at most 999999999s), so that path is bounded.
   - The behaviour change on rollback is also missing from the header (:104-107), the CHANGELOG entry and the runbook.
   - Fix: run the REGISTRY_WINDOW check for --rollback too, or fall back to the 1800s default on an invalid value. Then update the comment and the docs.

4. MINOR — scripts/promote-latest.mjs:1921. STEP 7 can now run silently for a long time. The README read-back announces its wait at :1983, but STEP 7 announces nothing. An operator who interrupts what looks like a hang recreates the LCLI-689 incident: Release uncut, read-back skipped.
   - Fix: before verifyTags, print a line like "re-reading latest for up to ${lagWindow}s".

5. MINOR — scripts/promote-latest.mjs:1929. The exit-1 remedy is incomplete. It says to run "the GitHub Release step by hand" once latest converges. But the same early return also skipped STEP 7's integrity check (verifyFinalLauncher) and the README read-back.
   - Fix: also list `npm view @opum-ai/lore@X dist.integrity` against the artifact, the read-back rerun command, or simply "re-run --promote" (the resume path re-reaches STEP 7 without republishing).

6. MINOR — scripts/promote-latest.mjs:1937-1938 vs :1929. Two kinds of read-lag exhaustion now get opposite remedies.
   - When tags never converge: "Nothing was rolled back: re-read".
   - When the integrity read stays absent or empty for the whole window (:1113, :1119): it sends the operator to `--rollback`. That makes sense for a different integrity, not for one npm never served.
   - Fix: for the not-found / no-integrity case, print the re-read remedy, and keep --rollback for an integrity mismatch.

7. MINOR — test/promote-latest.test.ts:3270-3321. No main-level test covers the `...waitOptions` wiring at :1934. The world only lags the dist-tags reads, so reverting :1934 to the old fixed 10 reads would stay green. The verifyFinalLauncher unit test at :2256 passes attempts explicitly.
   - Fix: add a world option that has probeVersion answer absent for N reads after the publish, then test it under window "30".

8. MINOR — test/promote-latest.test.ts:3308-3315. The non-converging test does not check claim 3.
   - Fix: assert the text "Nothing was rolled back", and that `w.writes` contains no restore (`dist-tag add …@${PRIOR} latest`).
   - By code read, claim 3 is TRUE. The :1927-1931 path returns 1 with no rollback() call: rollback is reached only from promote() on a failed write (:621) and from --rollback.

9. NOTE — scripts/promote-latest.mjs:661-665, 680-688. The window is a count of reads, not a deadline. Each round makes seven sequential `npm view` calls plus a 15s sleep, so 121 rounds take more than 1800s of wall time. The two STEP 7 halves each get a full window, one after the other, and the read-back gets a third.
   - Worst case on --promote is roughly 3×1800s plus read latency, about 1.5-2.5h. That is bounded: no unbounded loop on --promote.
   - defaultRun (:211) sets no execFile timeout, so a hung `npm view` would block indefinitely. That predates this PR.
   - No CI or job timeout applies. No workflow runs this script: .github/workflows/release.yml mentions it only in comments (:178, :1258, :1376, :1625, :1729, :1798). It is operator-run.
   - Optional: a deadline like readme-readback.sh's `deadline=$(( … + REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS ))` would make the printed "REGISTRY_WINDOW_SECONDS N" exact.

10. NOTE — docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md:1243-1245. It says step 7 re-reads "until each reads <version>", without naming the bound, the window variable, or what exit 1 there means and how to remedy it. Lines 1278-1282 describe the window only for the read-back. Fix: one sentence on step 7's window and its exit-1 remedy.

11. NOTE — .quest/tasks/LCLI-689.json implementation note. ensureGitHubRelease still makes one attempt, so an upstream HTTP 500 still leaves the Release uncut, at exit 3. That is outside AC0/AC1, but the note asks for it to be weighed. Consider a follow-up task.

Claims I could confirm by file read: claim 1 (default 1800 → 121 reads at 15s; explicit verifyOptions wins through the spread order at :1522-1525), claim 3, claim 4 as far as the text goes (an [Unreleased] ### Fixed entry exists at CHANGELOG.md:10-16, and [0.14.1] follows at :18), and claim 7's structure. The tests inject both clock and sleep: NAP sets sleep to a no-op, readback-readback.sh is stubbed by the world's bash handler, and nothing sleeps for real. The lag boundary pair (2 stale reads converge on read 3 of 3; 3 stale reads fail after 3) is tight, and the default-window case (50 stale reads → exit 0) would fail at the old 10 reads.

EXIT CODE (1 vs 3): exit 1 is correct and matches the script's own contract.
- Header :114-118 and README_READBACK_EXIT (:1148-1156) define 3 as "the promotion is COMPLETE and verified" and pair it with "Do NOT run --rollback".
- After a full window of wrong reads, STEP 7 has verified nothing. Exit 3 would print a false "verified" and forbid a rollback that may be the right remedy, for instance if a write was acknowledged but never applied.
- Exit 1 is "refused or failed; what moved … and the remedy are printed", and :1929 does print both.
- AC1: the right reading is that "writes all succeeded" is scoped by AC0's "while the npm read API catches up". From inside the run, a write never served within 30 minutes cannot be told apart from a write that never landed. So not cutting a GitHub Release marked latest on that path is correct, and AC1 is met for lag inside the window, which covers the 0.13.0 incident's "minutes later".

UNVERIFIED BY FILE READ
- Nothing in the publish or dist-tag write path changed. I had no diff. The current write sites (promote() :600-629, publishFinalLauncher, setTag :1873, launcherPublishArgs) look consistent, but I cannot say what the PR touched.
- What --rollback's verification used before this PR (assumed: verifyOptions with the default 10 reads), and therefore whether finding 3 is a regression or simply new.
- That the [0.14.1] CHANGELOG section is byte-identical to before.
- The mutation claim (derived attempts → 1 turns exactly those three tests red). By reading, all three would go red and readLagAttempts' unit test would stay green, but nothing was run.
- That tests, lint and typecheck pass on this SHA.
- Claim 6: QCLI-465 has no implemented fix, and quest-cli#530-#532 only file and record.

NEW FINDINGS (none blocking):
- NOTE, :1947 and :1957 against the resume path at :1789-1801 (code from before this diff, reached by the new remedies). On a resume, step 8 probes the launcher before anything moves. (a) If npm still serves it present with a null integrity, :1796 refuses with "needs a new version, not a rerun". That reports an unread value as a mismatch, the boundary MINOR 6 holds, and publishFinalLauncher at :1072 treats the same state as lag. (b) If npm still reads it absent while its dist-tags already show X, the resume plans a publish. That publish fails because the version exists, and promote() then restores every tag, rolling back a correct release. Only the remedy's "re-read first" ordering guards this. :1957 names the integrity to expect, but :1947 asks only for dist-tags. Fix as a follow-up: make :1796 treat !integrity the way :1072 does, and have :1947 also name the `npm view <launcher>@X dist.integrity` re-read.
- NOTE, :1937 and :1952. The announcement covers only the latest wait. verifyFinalLauncher's integrity wait is a second window of up to lagWindow with no announcement, so the silent worst case is about twice the printed bound. The --rollback restore wait (:1898) is not announced at all, and it grew from 10 reads to up to 1800s. Fix: one out() line before each.
- NOTE, test:3335-3353. The MINOR 3 test pins the printed fallback line but not the read bound: both cases converge on read 1, so a regression to readLagAttempts(window) would pass. The 121-read bound is verified only by reading :1529 and :1538.
- NOTE, CHANGELOG.md:16-17. "the exit-1 messages say nothing was rolled back" is not true of the integrity-MISMATCH exit 1, which prescribes --rollback. Wording only.
- NOTE, :1179 and :1529. "Bounded" means the --promote grammar, 0 to 999999999s. 999999999 is still accepted and gives about 6.7e7 reads (~31 years). This matches the leader's "same check --promote uses", so it is by design.
